title: Colcannon with Kale and a Butter Well
summary: Potatoes mashed with milk infused by butter-softened kale and spring onions, served with a pool of butter in a well.

ingredients.item: floury or all-rounder potatoes (such as Yukon Gold), peeled
fine sea salt or table salt, for the cooking water
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Boil the potatoes
steps.text: Put the potatoes and 1 tbsp salt in the saucepan, cover with water by 2.5 cm and bring to the boil. Simmer for 18-22 min, until a knife slides in and out with no resistance.

steps.title: Cook the greens
steps.text: Meanwhile strip the kale leaves from the stems, slice the stems thinly and cut the leaves into 2.5 cm pieces. Melt the 85 g butter in the frying pan over medium heat and cook the stems with 1 tbsp water, 1 tsp salt and the pepper for 6-8 min until soft. Add the leaves and spring onions for 1-2 min until wilted, then pour in the milk, bring to a simmer, take off the heat and cover; the warm milk picks up the flavour of the greens.

steps.title: Mash
steps.text: Drain the potatoes, return them to the pan and stir over low heat for 30 seconds to drive off moisture, which makes a fluffier mash. Strain the hot milk over them, keeping the greens back, and mash to the texture you like. Fold the greens through and taste for salt.

steps.title: Make the butter well
steps.text: Pile the colcannon into a warm bowl, press a deep well into the centre with the back of a spoon and drop in the 30 g butter. Serve as it melts into a golden pool.

tips: Floury or all-rounder potatoes give a light mash; waxy ones turn gluey.
Never mash in a food processor, which makes potatoes sticky.
Green cabbage works instead of kale.
Leftovers fry well into crisp potato cakes.
storage: Refrigerate covered up to 3 days. Reheat in a pan with a splash of milk, stirring, or in a covered dish in the oven, until piping hot (74 °C). Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
